subject: science

entries: Circular motion needs a centre-seeking push: a satellite stays on its circular path only because a force keeps pulling it towards the centre, and that force arrow always points at the centre wherever the satellite is.
slots.label: Circular motion needs a centre-seeking push
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: How big is the centre-seeking force: the acceleration is a = v^2/r and the force is F = mv^2/r, so doubling the speed quadruples the force while doubling the radius halves it.
slots.label: How big is the centre-seeking force
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: Gravity holds the Moon in orbit: Newton's law F = GMm/r^2 supplies exactly the centripetal force the Moon needs, so every orbit is a continuous fall towards the Earth that keeps missing it.
slots.label: Gravity holds the Moon in orbit
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: Geostationary orbits hover over one spot: with a period of exactly 24 hours above the equator and turning with the Earth, the satellite hangs motionless over one point while a drifting satellite falls behind.
slots.label: Geostationary orbits hover over one spot
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: Misconception: the fling-off force: there is no outward centrifugal fling - the body keeps going straight on the tangent while the seat pushes it inward, and that inward push is the real force.
slots.label: Misconception: the fling-off force
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: The resultant force toward the centre of the circle that keeps an object in circular motion: F = mv^2/r. It is a role played by a real force such as tension, friction or gravity, not an extra force.
slots.label: Centripetal force
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: The acceleration toward the centre of the circle, a = v^2/r, caused by the changing direction of the velocity even when the speed is constant.
slots.label: Centripetal acceleration
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: The attractive force between two masses given by Newton's law F = GMm/r^2, with G = 6.67 x 10^-11 N m^2 kg^-2: double the separation and the force falls to one quarter.
slots.label: Gravitation
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: A circular orbit above the equator, travelling west to east with period 24 hours, so the satellite stays fixed over one point on the equator.
slots.label: Geostationary orbit
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: The time for one complete orbit or revolution, T. For a circular orbit T = 2 pi r / v, and a geostationary period is exactly 24 hours.
slots.label: Period
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.
